The traversal SHALL walk the symbol-level adjacency produced by `build_view_model()` (`symbolEdges`) restricted to edges whose `ty` is `call` — `import` and every other edge type are dependencies, not calls, and SHALL NOT appear as callers or callees — using only the Python standard library and making no network requests. Each line SHALL show `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`, children SHALL be sorted by name then id, a node already on the current path SHALL be printed once with the suffix `(cycle)` and not expanded, and a parent whose children exceed `--hops` SHALL carry the suffix `(+<n> more)`. The output SHALL end with a single footer line `graph @ <sha7> · <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered`, one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language present, sorted by language name and joined with ` / `, with `<percent>` printed to exactly one decimal place as `Coverage.percent` returns it (for example `14.4%`, `37.0%`), unless `--no-coverage` is given. `<target>` SHALL resolve as exact node id, then unique symbol name, then module file path or basename (rooting the tree at the module with its own symbols as hop 1). Exit codes SHALL be `0` success, `1` input or IO error, `2` target not found, `3` target ambiguous (candidate ids listed on stderr, one per line, sorted). Output SHALL be byte-identical across runs for a fixed graph and arguments.\n\n#### Scenario: Callees tree for a symbol\n\n- **WHEN** `build_atlas.py --tree <symbol-id>` runs against a graph containing that symbol\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL start with the symbol's line and list its callees indented two spaces per hop, sorted by name\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0`\n\n#### Scenario: Callers tree with hop cap\n\n- **WHEN** `--direction in --hops 1` is given for a symbol with callers two hops away\n- **THEN** only direct callers SHALL be printed\n- **AND** each printed caller that has further callers SHALL carry a `(+<n> more)` suffix\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call edges are excluded\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `A imports C`, and `--tree A --direction both` runs\n- **THEN** `B` SHALL be listed under `callees:`\n- **AND** `C` SHALL NOT appear anywhere in the output\n\n#### Scenario: Cycle is printed once\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `B calls A` and `--tree A --hops 4` runs\n- **THEN** `A` SHALL appear under `B` exactly once with the suffix `(cycle)`\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT be expanded further\n\n#### Scenario: File target gives the aggregated module view\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <file-basename>` names a module in the graph\n- **THEN** the root line SHALL be the module and hop 1 SHALL be the module's own symbols\n- **AND** subsequent hops SHALL follow those symbols' `call` edges\n\n#### Scenario: Unknown target exits 2\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a symbol that is not in the graph\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `2`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain `not found`\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous target exits 3\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a bare symbol name matching several node ids\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `3`, distinct from not-found\n- **AND** stderr SHALL list the candidate ids, one per line, sorted\n\n#### Scenario: Deterministic output\n\n- **WHEN** the same `--tree` invocation runs twice against the same graph file\n- **THEN** the two stdout outputs SHALL be byte-identical\n\n#### Scenario: Coverage footer matches the page banner\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` runs without `--no-coverage`\n- **THEN** the footer percentages SHALL equal the `Coverage.percent` values `build_view_model()` computes for the same repository root\n\n#### Scenario: Default hops and direction\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target>` is invoked with neither `--hops` nor `--direction`\n- **THEN** the traversal SHALL use `--hops 2` and `--direction out`\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0` for a resolvable target\n\n#### Scenario: Hops above four are clamped\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --hops 9` is given\n- **THEN** the effective hop cap SHALL be `4`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain a note that the value was clamped\n\n#### Scenario: No-coverage suppresses the footer\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --no-coverage` runs\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL omit the `graph @` coverage footer line\n\n#### Scenario: Input or IO error exits 1\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` cannot read the graph file (missing path via `--graph`, or unreadable IO)\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `1`\n\n\n#### specs/skill-workflow/spec.md\n## ADDED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: Visual Code Explainer Skill\n\nThe repository SHALL provide a user-invocable, prompt-only skill `explain-code` that answers a narrow question about the code with the smallest visual form that makes the key point clear, drawn from a fixed catalogue: indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree with one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, and structural (tree) diff. The skill SHALL keep prose brief, SHALL place each visual next to the short text it supports, and SHALL include only the calls, files, and boundaries the current question needs. The skill's `SKILL.md` SHALL be an index of at most 150 lines that links directly to one `references/<form>.md` file per visual form, with no nested reference files. In this version the skill SHALL NOT write HTML files, SHALL NOT write any file, and SHALL NOT open a browser.\n\n#### Scenario: Narrow question answered with the smallest visual\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks how a specific function, module, or message path works or connects\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL reply with exactly one visual form from the catalogue and at most three sentences of prose\n- **AND** every node in the visual SHALL carry its file location\n\n#### Scenario: Whole-repository question redirected\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL NOT render a repository-wide tree\n- **AND** it SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` as the tool for that question and stop\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive disclosure layout\n\n- **WHEN** the skill directory is inspected\n- **THEN** `SKILL.md` SHALL be at most 150 lines\n- **AND** each catalogue form SHALL have its own `references/<form>.md` reachable by a direct link from `SKILL.md`\n- **AND** no reference file SHALL link to a further reference file\n\n#### Scenario: No file or browser side effects\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers any question\n- **THEN** it SHALL emit text and Mermaid inline in the reply only\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT create, modify, or open any file\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure\n\nBefore sketching a call tree, the skill SHALL determine graph freshness by running the read-only `run_architecture.py --check` from the co-installed `refresh-architecture` skill via `<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/run_architecture.py`, treating exit code `0` alone as fresh (any non-zero exit means ungrounded; the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh). When fresh, the skill SHALL obtain callers and callees from `build_atlas.py --tree` (co-installed `codebase-atlas`) and SHALL build the call tree only from nodes that `build_atlas.py --tree` returns. When `--tree` exits `3` (ambiguous target), the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant, and SHALL NOT fall back to source reading or sketch a tree. When stale, absent, or failing (including `--tree` exit `2`), the skill SHALL read source directly and label the sketch unverified. Every sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted) SHALL end with exactly one disclosure line: `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered` when grounded (coverage list taken from the `--tree` footer by copying the substring after `· ` and before the trailing ` covered`, then re-appending ` covered`, preserving language order and ` / ` separators), or `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)` when not, where `<reason>` is chosen by first-match order: `graph absent` (script or graph missing before `--check`), `graph check failed` (`--check` could not be spawned, or `--tree` exits `1` after a fresh `--check`), `graph stale` (`--check` ran and exited non-zero), `symbol not in graph` (`--tree` exited `2`), or `form not graph-backed` (non-call-tree catalogue form). Ambiguous-symbol clarification replies and whole-repository redirect replies SHALL NOT carry a `Grounding:` line. Only a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` MAY use the grounded form; other catalogue forms SHALL use `form not graph-backed`. The skill SHALL NOT run a refresh, `--ensure`, or the analysis pipeline itself.\n\n#### Scenario: Fresh graph grounds the call tree\n\n- **WHEN** `run_architecture.py --check` exits `0` and the question names a symbol present in the graph\n- **THEN** the call tree SHALL contain only nodes returned by `build_atlas.py --tree`\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; …` with per-language coverage percentages copied from the `--tree` footer per the substring rule above\n\n#### Scenario: Stale or absent graph falls back to source\n\n- **WHEN** `run_architecture.py --check` exits non-zero, or the script or graph file is missing\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL still answer, drawing the sketch from the source files it reads\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)` with reason `graph stale`, `graph absent`, or `graph check failed` per the first-match order above\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT invoke `--ensure` or the analysis pipeline\n\n#### Scenario: Symbol outside graph coverage\n\n- **WHEN** the graph is fresh but `build_atlas.py --tree` exits `2` (target not found) for the requested symbol\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL fall back to source reading for that symbol\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (symbol not in graph)`\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call-tree form is not graph-backed\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers with a catalogue form other than a call tree\n- **THEN** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (form not graph-backed)`\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT claim the grounded `graph @` form for that reply\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing\n\n- **WHEN** the graph is fresh and `build_atlas.py --tree` exits `3` (ambiguous name) for the requested symbol\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT fall back to source reading or sketch a tree for any candidate\n- **AND** the reply SHALL NOT include a `Grounding:` line\n\n#### Scenario: Whole-repository redirect has no disclosure line\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` and stop\n- **AND** the reply SHALL NOT include a `Grounding:` line\n\n#### Scenario: Disclosure line present on every sketching answer\n\n- **WHEN** the skill produces a sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted), grounded or not\n- **THEN** the final line of the reply SHALL begin with `Grounding:`\n- **AND** the reply SHALL contain exactly one such line\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Frontmatter Without Triggers\n\nThe `explain-code` `SKILL.md` frontmatter SHALL declare `name`, `description`, `category: Architecture`, `tags`, `user_invocable: true`, and `related: [codebase-atlas, refresh-architecture]`, and SHALL NOT declare a `triggers:` key. The `description` SHALL state, in third person, both what the skill does and when to use it, including that whole-repository views belong to `codebase-atlas`. The skill's `test_skill_md.py` SHALL assert the declared keys explicitly rather than through the shared `assert_required_keys_present` helper while that helper still requires `triggers`, so the test passes whether or not `rewrite-skill-frontmatter` has landed. The `SKILL.md` SHALL end with the `## Common Rationalizations`, `## Red Flags`, and `## Verification` sections required of user-invocable skills.\n\n#### Scenario: Frontmatter valid in both orderings\n\n- **WHEN** `skills/tests/explain-code/test_skill_md.py` runs before or after `rewrite-skill-frontmatter` merges\n- **THEN** it SHALL pass in both states\n- **AND** it SHALL fail if any of `name`, `description`, `category`, `tags`, `user_invocable`, or `related` is missing or empty\n\n#### Scenario: Description carries the trigger condition\n\n- **WHEN** the frontmatter `description` is read\n- **THEN** it SHALL name the capability (visual explanation of a specific piece of code) and the use condition (a narrow question about how code works or connects)\n- **AND** it SHALL direct whole-repository requests to `codebase-atlas`\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Distribution Wiring\n\n`skills/install-manifest.json` SHALL declare `\"explain-code\": {\"distribution\": \"portable\"}` and a `cross_skill_dependencies` entry `\"explain-code\": [\"codebase-atlas\", \"refresh-architecture\"]`. `skills/pyproject.toml` `testpaths` SHALL list `tests/explain-code`. Output SHALL be byte-identical across runs for a fixed graph and arguments.\n\n#### Scenario: Callees tree for a symbol\n\n- **WHEN** `build_atlas.py --tree <symbol-id>` runs against a graph containing that symbol\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL start with the symbol's line and list its callees indented two spaces per hop, sorted by name\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0`\n\n#### Scenario: Callers tree with hop cap\n\n- **WHEN** `--direction in --hops 1` is given for a symbol with callers two hops away\n- **THEN** only direct callers SHALL be printed\n- **AND** each printed caller that has further callers SHALL carry a `(+<n> more)` suffix\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call edges are excluded\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `A imports C`, and `--tree A --direction both` runs\n- **THEN** `B` SHALL be listed under `callees:`\n- **AND** `C` SHALL NOT appear anywhere in the output\n\n#### Scenario: Cycle is printed once\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `B calls A` and `--tree A --hops 4` runs\n- **THEN** `A` SHALL appear under `B` exactly once with the suffix `(cycle)`\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT be expanded further\n\n#### Scenario: File target gives the aggregated module view\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <file-basename>` names a module in the graph\n- **THEN** the root line SHALL be the module and hop 1 SHALL be the module's own symbols\n- **AND** subsequent hops SHALL follow those symbols' `call` edges\n\n#### Scenario: Unknown target exits 2\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a symbol that is not in the graph\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `2`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain `not found`\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous target exits 3\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a bare symbol name matching several node ids\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `3`, distinct from not-found\n- **AND** stderr SHALL list the candidate ids, one per line, sorted\n\n#### Scenario: Deterministic output\n\n- **WHEN** the same `--tree` invocation runs twice against the same graph file\n- **THEN** the two stdout outputs SHALL be byte-identical\n\n#### Scenario: Coverage footer matches the page banner\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` runs without `--no-coverage`\n- **THEN** the footer percentages SHALL equal the `Coverage.percent` values `build_view_model()` computes for the same repository root\n\n#### Scenario: Default hops and direction\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target>` is invoked with neither `--hops` nor `--direction`\n- **THEN** the traversal SHALL use `--hops 2` and `--direction out`\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0` for a resolvable target\n\n#### Scenario: Hops above four are clamped\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --hops 9` is given\n- **THEN** the effective hop cap SHALL be `4`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain a note that the value was clamped\n\n#### Scenario: No-coverage suppresses the footer\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --no-coverage` runs\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL omit the `graph @` coverage footer line\n\n#### Scenario: Input or IO error exits 1\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` cannot read the graph file (missing path via `--graph`, or unreadable IO)\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `1`\n\n\n#### specs/skill-workflow/spec.md\n## ADDED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: Visual Code Explainer Skill\n\nThe repository SHALL provide a user-invocable, prompt-only skill `explain-code` that answers a narrow question about the code with the smallest visual form that makes the key point clear, drawn from a fixed catalogue: indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree with one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, and structural (tree) diff. The skill SHALL keep prose brief, SHALL place each visual next to the short text it supports, and SHALL include only the calls, files, and boundaries the current question needs. The skill's `SKILL.md` SHALL be an index of at most 150 lines that links directly to one `references/<form>.md` file per visual form, with no nested reference files. In this version the skill SHALL NOT write HTML files, SHALL NOT write any file, and SHALL NOT open a browser.\n\n#### Scenario: Narrow question answered with the smallest visual\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks how a specific function, module, or message path works or connects\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL reply with exactly one visual form from the catalogue and at most three sentences of prose\n- **AND** every node in the visual SHALL carry its file location\n\n#### Scenario: Whole-repository question redirected\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL NOT render a repository-wide tree\n- **AND** it SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` as the tool for that question and stop\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive disclosure layout\n\n- **WHEN** the skill directory is inspected\n- **THEN** `SKILL.md` SHALL be at most 150 lines\n- **AND** each catalogue form SHALL have its own `references/<form>.md` reachable by a direct link from `SKILL.md`\n- **AND** no reference file SHALL link to a further reference file\n\n#### Scenario: No file or browser side effects\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers any question\n- **THEN** it SHALL emit text and Mermaid inline in the reply only\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT create, modify, or open any file\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure\n\nBefore sketching a call tree, the skill SHALL determine graph freshness by running the read-only `run_architecture.py --check` from the co-installed `refresh-architecture` skill via `<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/run_architecture.py`, treating exit code `0` alone as fresh (any non-zero exit means ungrounded; the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh). When fresh, the skill SHALL obtain callers and callees from `build_atlas.py --tree` (co-installed `codebase-atlas`) and SHALL build the call tree only from nodes that `build_atlas.py --tree` returns. When `--tree` exits `3` (ambiguous target), the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant, and SHALL NOT fall back to source reading or sketch a tree. When stale, absent, or failing (including `--tree` exit `2`), the skill SHALL read source directly and label the sketch unverified. Every sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted) SHALL end with exactly one disclosure line: `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered` when grounded (coverage list taken from the `--tree` footer by copying the substring after `· ` and before the trailing ` covered`, then re-appending ` covered`, preserving language order and ` / ` separators), or `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)` when not, where `<reason>` is chosen by first-match order: `graph absent` (script or graph missing before `--check`), `graph check failed` (`--check` could not be spawned, or `--tree` exits `1` after a fresh `--check`), `graph stale` (`--check` ran and exited non-zero), `symbol not in graph` (`--tree` exited `2`), or `form not graph-backed` (non-call-tree catalogue form). Ambiguous-symbol clarification replies and whole-repository redirect replies SHALL NOT carry a `Grounding:` line. Only a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` MAY use the grounded form; other catalogue forms SHALL use `form not graph-backed`. The skill SHALL NOT run a refresh, `--ensure`, or the analysis pipeline itself.\n\n#### Scenario: Fresh graph grounds the call tree\n\n- **WHEN** `run_architecture.py --check` exits `0` and the question names a symbol present in the graph\n- **THEN** the call tree SHALL contain only nodes returned by `build_atlas.py --tree`\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: graph @ Scenario: Non-call-tree form is not graph-backed\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers with a catalogue form other than a call tree\n- **THEN** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (form not graph-backed)`\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT claim the grounded `graph @` form for that reply\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing\n\n- **WHEN** the graph is fresh and `build_atlas.py --tree` exits `3` (ambiguous name) for the requested symbol\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant\n- **AND** the skill line\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` and stop\n- **AND** the reply SHALL NOT include a `Grounding:` line\n\n#### Scenario: Disclosure line present on every sketching answer\n\n- **WHEN** the skill produces a sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted), grounded or {"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-ce6e479320d041299a36ab00b3225de9","toolName":"read","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design — add-visual-code-explainer\n\n## Context\n\nTwo visualization skills exist and both are artifact-first: `codebase-atlas`\nrenders the whole graph to one HTML page; `refresh-architecture` emits Mermaid\nviews at fixed zoom levels. Neither answers a narrow question quickly. The\nsource of the adopted pattern (humanlayer `show-me`, MIT) is prompt-only and\nungrounded. This design adds the question-first entry point while keeping the\nrepository's provenance and coverage principles intact.\n\nConstraints inherited from in-flight changes (see `proposal.md` → Impact):\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` removes `triggers:`; `apply-progressive-disclosure-\noversized-skills` caps `SKILL.md` at 500 lines and references at one level;\n`invert-skill-test-suite-to-behavioural` wants three behavioural scenarios per\nuser-invocable skill; `collect-uncollected-skill-tests` requires a `testpaths`\nentry and forbids bare-named helper modules that collide across skills.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Prompt-only skill; the only new code is an atlas flag\n\n`skills/explain-code/` contains `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md`, no `scripts/`.\nGrounding calls `<skill-base-dir>/../codebase-atlas/scripts/build_atlas.py\n--tree`. Rationale: the catalogue works *because* it is prose (Approach 1 vs 2\nin the proposal); the one place determinism pays is the call tree, and the\natlas already holds the symbol adjacency (`build_view_model()[\"symbolEdges\"]`).\n\n### D2 — Freshness is decided by the existing `--check` contract\n\nThe skill runs `python3 \"<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/\nrun_architecture.py\" --check` and treats **exit 0 only** as fresh. Any\nnon-zero exit — the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh, and\nother failures are also non-zero — a missing script, or a missing graph all\nmean *ungrounded*. Do **not** confuse this with `build_atlas.py --check`,\nwhich uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page; that flag is unrelated to\nexplain-code freshness. Rationale: `run_architecture.py --check` is the\nread-only half of the `architecture-refresh` contract; re-deriving freshness\nfrom `git_sha` in prose would be a second, weaker definition. The skill\n**never** runs `--ensure` or the full pipeline (proposal: \"never triggers a\nrefresh on its own\").\n\n### D3 — `--tree` output format\n\n```\nbuild_atlas.py --tree <target> [--hops N] [--direction out|in|both] [--graph PATH]\n```\n\n- Root line: `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`.\n- Children indented two spaces per hop, sorted by `name` then `id`; direction\n  `out` lists callees (`call` edges where the node is `s`), `in` lists callers, `both`\n  prints two labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`.\n- A node already printed on the current path is emitted once with the suffix\n  `(cycle)` and not expanded. A node beyond `--hops` is not printed; the parent\n  line gets the suffix `(+<n> more)` so truncation is visible.\n- `--hops` default `2`, maximum `4` (matches the page's hop slider,\n  `atlas_render.py`). Values above 4 are clamped with a stderr note.\n- Only edges with `ty == \"call\"` are walked (singular, the spelling the graph\n  uses). `symbolEdges` carries every edge type — the committed graph holds both\n  `call` and `import` edges — and an import is a dependency, not a call: walking\n  it would report importers as callers and corrupt the grounded output. A\n  dependency-tree mode over `import` edges is out of scope for this change.\n- Trailing footer, one line: `graph @ <sha7> · python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`:\n  one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language, sorted by language name, joined\n  with ` / `, percent to one decimal place (the `Coverage.percent` value\n  itself, never re-rounded, so it stays equal to the page banner), a single\n  trailing `covered`. Percentages are\n  taken from `build_view_model(measure=True)` — the same `Coverage`\n  values the page banner uses. `--no-coverage` suppresses it.\n\nDeterminism: children sorted, no timestamps, no random ids. Byte-identical for a\nfixed graph and arguments (NFR \"Determinism\").\n\n### D4 — Target resolution\n\n`<target>` resolves in this order and stops at the first hit: exact node `id`;\nunique symbol `name`; a file path or basename matching a module, in which case\nthe root is the module and hop 1 is the module's own symbols (aggregated view,\nmirroring the page's \"selecting a file gives the aggregated module view\").\nNo match exits `2` with `not found`. Ambiguous names print the candidate ids to\nstderr (one per line, sorted) and exit `3`. The two stay distinct because the\nskill must react differently: a missing symbol falls back to source reading, but\nan ambiguous one exists in the graph, so a source fallback would silently answer\nabout a guessed symbol; the skill asks which candidate was meant instead. Exit\n`1` remains input/IO errors, `0` success. Exit `3` is new for `--tree`.\n`build_atlas.py --check` already uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page;\n`--check` and `--tree` never combine on one invocation.\n\n### D5 — Disclosure line\n\nEvery **sketching** reply (a catalogue visual was emitted, grounded or not)\nends with exactly one line, never omitted, never collapsed. Two reply shapes\nare explicit exceptions and MUST NOT carry a `Grounding:` line:\n\n- **Ambiguous-symbol clarification** — `--tree` exited `3`; the skill lists\n  candidate ids and asks which was meant (no visual, no source fallback).\n- **Whole-repository redirect** — the skill names `/codebase-atlas` and stops\n  (no visual).\n\nSketching replies use one of:\n\n- grounded call tree:\n  `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`\n  Take the `--tree` footer from D3, copy the substring after `· ` and before\n  the trailing ` covered`, then re-append ` covered`. That substring is the\n  coverage list — same language order, ` / ` separators, and one-decimal\n  percents — so the disclosure and footer cannot drift. The line uses `; `\n  after the sha (not the footer's `·`) and always starts with `Grounding:`.\n- ungrounded / non-graph-backed:\n  `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)`\n  where `<reason>` is exactly one of (decision order; first match wins):\n  - `graph absent` — before invoking `--check`, the skill finds the\n    `--check` script or the graph file missing\n  - `graph check failed` — the skill could not spawn/run `--check`\n    (OSError / exception before an exit code), or a subsequent `--tree`\n    exits `1` (input/IO) after a fresh `--check`\n  - `graph stale` — `--check` ran and exited non-zero (including exit `1`\n    for stale provenance and any other non-zero the script returns)\n  - `symbol not in graph` — `--tree` exited `2`\n  - `form not graph-backed` — reply used a catalogue form other than a\n    call tree (component/file/sequence/structural-diff are model-authored)\n\nOnly a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` may use the\ngrounded form. The percentages are the atlas's optimistic upper bound and\nthe grounding reference says so.\n\n### D6 — Frontmatter without `triggers:`; explicit key test\n\n`SKILL.md` frontmatter: `name`, `description` (third person, capability + when\nto use), `category: Architecture`, `tags`, `user_invocable: true`,\n`related: [codebase-atlas, refresh-architecture]`. `test_skill_md.py` asserts\nthose keys directly and does **not** call `assert_required_keys_present` (whose\n`REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_KEYS` still lists `triggers`). When\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` lands and updates that tuple, the test can switch\nback to the shared helper; until then both orderings pass (NFR\n\"Compatibility\"). Independently of the\nharness, three **deterministic** tests always run in CI and encode the same\nthree behaviours at the level the prompt can be checked without an LLM:\n\n1. `SKILL.md` / grounding reference instruct the disclosure line for grounded\n   and ungrounded sketching paths (both D5 templates present; the closed\n   ungrounded reason set `graph stale|absent|check failed`, `symbol not in\n   graph`, `form not graph-backed` present as exact tokens; the\n   footer→disclosure mapping documented — copy after `· ` / before trailing\n   ` covered`, re-append ` covered`, use `; ` after the sha; clarification\n   and redirect replies exempt from `Grounding:`).\n2. `SKILL.md` instructs redirecting whole-repository questions to\n   `/codebase-atlas` (string present, and the atlas is in `related:`).\n3. `SKILL.md` instructs never running `--ensure` or the analysis pipeline\n   (D2/D9 strings present; the skill cannot silently trigger a refresh).\n\nThe fourth behaviour — \"a grounded call tree cannot invent symbols\" — is\nasserted where the code lives: `tests/codebase-atlas/test_atlas_tree.py`\nchecks that every node printed for the `tiny_graph` fixture matches a\nfixture node by `(name, file)` (the tree format emits name/file/kind, not\nnode ids). Keeping it there lets `wp-skill` and `wp-atlas-tree` run in\nparallel without `wp-skill` importing code it does not own.\n\nRationale: the inversion change is 0/10 tasks; this change must be green on\ntoday's CI and must not block on it.\n\n### D8 — Module layout inside the atlas\n\nThe BFS and formatter live in `skills/codebase-atlas/scripts/atlas_tree.py`\n(prefixed name; `collect-uncollected-skill-tests` forbids bare `tree`/`models`\nnames that collide across skills under flat collection). `build_atlas.py`\ngains the flags and dispatches to it before the render path, after\n`build_view_model()`.\n\n### D9 — What the skill refuses\n\n- It does not write files. Neither answers a narrow question quickly. The\nsource of the adopted pattern (humanlayer `show-me`, MIT) is prompt-only and\nungrounded. This design adds the question-first entry point while keeping the\nrepository's provenance and coverage principles intact.\n\nConstraints inherited from in-flight changes (see `proposal.md` → Impact):\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` removes `triggers:`; `apply-progressive-disclosure-\noversized-skills` caps `SKILL.md` at 500 lines and references at one level;\n`invert-skill-test-suite-to-behavioural` wants three behavioural scenarios per\nuser-invocable skill; `collect-uncollected-skill-tests` requires a `testpaths`\nentry and forbids bare-named helper modules that collide across skills.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Prompt-only skill; the only new code is an atlas flag\n\n`skills/explain-code/` contains `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md`, no `scripts/`.\nGrounding calls `<skill-base-dir>/../codebase-atlas/scripts/build_atlas.py\n--tree`. Rationale: the catalogue works *because* it is prose (Approach 1 vs 2\nin the proposal); the one place determinism pays is the call tree, and the\natlas already holds the symbol adjacency (`build_view_model()[\"symbolEdges\"]`).\n\n### D2 — Freshness is decided by the existing `--check` contract\n\nThe skill runs `python3 \"<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/\nrun_architecture.py\" --check` and treats **exit 0 only** as fresh. Any\nnon-zero exit — the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh, and\nother failures are also non-zero — a missing script, or a missing graph all\nmean *ungrounded*. Do **not** confuse this with `build_atlas.py --check`,\nwhich uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page; that flag is unrelated to\nexplain-code freshness. Rationale: `run_architecture.py --check` is the\nread-only half of the `architecture-refresh` contract; re-deriving freshness\nfrom `git_sha` in prose would be a second, weaker definition. The skill\n**never** runs `--ensure` or the full pipeline (proposal: \"never triggers a\nrefresh on its own\").\n\n### D3 — `--tree` output format\n\n```\nbuild_atlas.py --tree <target> [--hops N] [--direction out|in|both] [--graph PATH]\n```\n\n- Root line: `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`.\n- Children indented two spaces per hop, sorted by `name` then `id`; direction\n  `out` lists callees (`call` edges where the node is `s`), `in` lists callers, `both`\n  prints two labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`.\n- A node already printed on the current path is emitted once with the suffix\n  `(cycle)` and not expanded. A node beyond `--hops` is not printed; the parent\n  line gets the suffix `(+<n> more)` so truncation is visible.\n- `--hops` default `2`, maximum `4` (matches the page's hop slider,\n  `atlas_render.py`). Values above 4 are clamped with a stderr note.\n- Only edges with `ty == \"call\"` are walked (singular, the spelling the graph\n  uses). `symbolEdges` carries every edge type — the committed graph holds both\n  `call` and `import` edges — and an import is a dependency, not a call: walking\n  it would report importers as callers and corrupt the grounded output. A\n  dependency-tree mode over `import` edges is out of scope for this change.\n- Trailing footer, one line: `graph @ <sha7> · python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`:\n  one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language, sorted by language name, joined\n  with ` / `, percent to one decimal place (the `Coverage.percent` value\n  itself, never re-rounded, so it stays equal to the page banner), a single\n  trailing `covered`. Percentages are\n  taken from `build_view_model(measure=True)` — the same `Coverage`\n  values the page banner uses. `--no-coverage` suppresses it.\n\nDeterminism: children sorted, no timestamps, no random ids. Byte-identical for a\nfixed graph and arguments (NFR \"Determinism\").\n\n### D4 — Target resolution\n\n`<target>` resolves in this order and stops at the first hit: exact node `id`;\nunique symbol `name`; a file path or basename matching a module, in which case\nthe root is the module and hop 1 is the module's own symbols (aggregated view,\nmirroring the page's \"selecting a file gives the aggregated module view\").\nNo match exits `2` with `not found`. Ambiguous names print the candidate ids to\nstderr (one per line, sorted) and exit `3`. The two stay distinct because the\nskill must react differently: a missing symbol falls back to source reading, but\nan ambiguous one exists in the graph, so a source fallback would silently answer\nabout a guessed symbol; the skill asks which candidate was meant instead. Exit\n`1` remains input/IO errors, `0` success. Exit `3` is new for `--tree`.\n`build_atlas.py --check` already uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page;\n`--check` and `--tree` never combine on one invocation.\n\n### D5 — Disclosure line\n\nEvery **sketching** reply (a catalogue visual was emitted, grounded or not)\nends with exactly one line, never omitted, never collapsed. Two reply shapes\nare explicit exceptions and MUST NOT carry a `Grounding:` line:\n\n- **Ambiguous-symbol clarification** — `--tree` exited `3`; the skill lists\n  candidate ids and asks which was meant (no visual, no source fallback).\n- **Whole-repository redirect** — the skill names `/codebase-atlas` and stops\n  (no visual).\n\nSketching replies use one of:\n\n- grounded call tree:\n  `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`\n  Take the `--tree` footer from D3, copy the substring after `· ` and before\n  the trailing ` covered`, then re-append ` covered`. That substring is the\n  coverage list — same language order, ` / ` separators, and one-decimal\n  percents — so the disclosure and footer cannot drift. The line uses `; `\n  after the sha (not the footer's `·`) and always starts with `Grounding:`.\n- ungrounded / non-graph-backed:\n  `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)`\n  where `<reason>` is exactly one of (decision order; first match wins):\n  - `graph absent` — before invoking `--check`, the skill finds the\n    `--check` script or the graph file missing\n  - `graph check failed` — the skill could not spawn/run `--check`\n    (OSError / exception before an exit code), or a subsequent `--tree`\n    exits `1` (input/IO) after a fresh `--check`\n  - `graph stale` — `--check` ran and exited non-zero (including exit `1`\n    for stale provenance and any other non-zero the script returns)\n  - `symbol not in graph` — `--tree` exited `2`\n  - `form not graph-backed` — reply used a catalogue form other than a\n    call tree (component/file/sequence/structural-diff are model-authored)\n\nOnly a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` may use the\ngrounded form. The percentages are the atlas's optimistic upper bound and\nthe grounding reference says so.\n\n### D6 — Frontmatter without `triggers:`; explicit key test\n\n`SKILL.md` frontmatter: `name`, `description` (third person, capability + when\nto use), `category: Architecture`, `tags`, `user_invocable: true`,\n`related: [codebase-atlas, refresh-architecture]`. `test_skill_md.py` asserts\nthose keys directly and does **not** call `assert_required_keys_present` (whose\n`REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_KEYS` still lists `triggers`). When\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` lands and updates that tuple, the test can switch\nback to the shared helper; until then both orderings pass (NFR\n\"Compatibility\"). The description carries the trigger condition — \"when the\nuser asks how a specific piece of the code works or connects, not for a\nwhole-repository view (use codebase-atlas for that)\".\n\n### D7 — Behavioural scenarios: harness-shaped, CI-wired at the deterministic edge\n\nThree scenarios are authored as fixtures under `skills/tests/explain-code/scenarios/`\nin the trajectory-scenario harness format when that harness is available in\nthe checkout; otherwise as pytest tests marked `e2e`. Neither answers a narrow question quickly. The\nsource of the adopted pattern (humanlayer `show-me`, MIT) is prompt-only and\nungrounded. This design adds the question-first entry point while keeping the\nrepository's provenance and coverage principles intact.\n\nConstraints inherited from in-flight changes (see `proposal.md` → Impact):\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` removes `triggers:`; `apply-progressive-disclosure-\noversized-skills` caps `SKILL.md` at 500 lines and references at one level;\n`invert-skill-test-suite-to-behavioural` wants three behavioural scenarios per\nuser-invocable skill; `collect-uncollected-skill-tests` requires a `testpaths`\nentry and forbids bare-named helper modules that collide across skills.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Prompt-only skill; the only new code is an atlas flag\n\n`skills/explain-code/` contains `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md`, no `scripts/`.\nGrounding calls `<skill-base-dir>/../codebase-atlas/scripts/build_atlas.py\n--tree`. Rationale: the catalogue works *because* it is prose (Approach 1 vs 2\nin the proposal); the one place determinism pays is the call tree, and the\natlas already holds the symbol adjacency (`build_view_model()[\"symbolEdges\"]`).\n\n### D2 — Freshness is decided by the existing `--check` contract\n\nThe skill runs `python3 \"<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/\nrun_architecture.py\" --check` and treats **exit 0 only** as fresh. Any\nnon-zero exit — the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh, and\nother failures are also non-zero — a missing script, or a missing graph all\nmean *ungrounded*. Do **not** confuse this with `build_atlas.py --check`,\nwhich uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page; that flag is unrelated to\nexplain-code freshness. Rationale: `run_architecture.py --check` is the\nread-only half of the `architecture-refresh` contract; re-deriving freshness\nfrom `git_sha` in prose would be a second, weaker definition. The skill\n**never** runs `--ensure` or the full pipeline (proposal: \"never triggers a\nrefresh on its own\").\n\n### D3 — `--tree` output format\n\n```\nbuild_atlas.py --tree <target> [--hops N] [--direction out|in|both] [--graph PATH]\n```\n\n- Root line: `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`.\n- Children indented two spaces per hop, sorted by `name` then `id`; direction\n  `out` lists callees (`call` edges where the node is `s`), `in` lists callers, `both`\n  prints two labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`.\n- A node already printed on the current path is emitted once with the suffix\n  `(cycle)` and not expanded. A node beyond `--hops` is not printed; the parent\n  line gets the suffix `(+<n> more)` so truncation is visible.\n- `--hops` default `2`, maximum `4` (matches the page's hop slider,\n  `atlas_render.py`). Values above 4 are clamped with a stderr note.\n- Only edges with `ty == \"call\"` are walked (singular, the spelling the graph\n  uses). `symbolEdges` carries every edge type — the committed graph holds both\n  `call` and `import` edges — and an import is a dependency, not a call: walking\n  it would report importers as callers and corrupt the grounded output. A\n  dependency-tree mode over `import` edges is out of scope for this change.\n- Trailing footer, one line: `graph @ <sha7> · python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`:\n  one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language, sorted by language name, joined\n  with ` / `, percent to one decimal place (the `Coverage.percent` value\n  itself, never re-rounded, so it stays equal to the page banner), a single\n  trailing `covered`. Percentages are\n  taken from `build_view_model(measure=True)` — the same `Coverage`\n  values the page banner uses. `--no-coverage` suppresses it.\n\nDeterminism: children sorted, no timestamps, no random ids. Byte-identical for a\nfixed graph and arguments (NFR \"Determinism\").\n\n### D4 — Target resolution\n\n`<target>` resolves in this order and stops at the first hit: exact node `id`;\nunique symbol `name`; a file path or basename matching a module, in which case\nthe root is the module and hop 1 is the module's own symbols (aggregated view,\nmirroring the page's \"selecting a file gives the aggregated module view\").\nNo match exits `2` with `not found`. Ambiguous names print the candidate ids to\nstderr (one per line, sorted) and exit `3`. The two stay distinct because the\nskill must react differently: a missing symbol falls back to source reading, but\nan ambiguous one exists in the graph, so a source fallback would silently answer\nabout a guessed symbol; the skill asks which candidate was meant instead. Exit\n`1` remains input/IO errors, `0` success. Exit `3` is new for `--tree`.\n`build_atlas.py --check` already uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page;\n`--check` and `--tree` never combine on one invocation.\n\n### D5 — Disclosure line\n\nEvery **sketching** reply (a catalogue visual was emitted, grounded or not)\nends with exactly one line, never omitted, never collapsed. Two reply shapes\nare explicit exceptions and MUST NOT carry a `Grounding:` line:\n\n- **Ambiguous-symbol clarification** — `--tree` exited `3`; the skill lists\n  candidate ids and asks which was meant (no visual, no source fallback).\n- **Whole-repository redirect** — the skill names `/codebase-atlas` and stops\n  (no visual).\n\nSketching replies use one of:\n\n- grounded call tree:\n  `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`\n  Take the `--tree` footer from D3, copy the substring after `· ` and before\n  the trailing ` covered`, then re-append ` covered`. That substring is the\n  coverage list — same language order, ` / ` separators, and one-decimal\n  percents — so the disclosure and footer cannot drift. The line uses `; `\n  after the sha (not the footer's `·`) and always starts with `Grounding:`.\n- ungrounded / non-graph-backed:\n  `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)`\n  where `<reason>` is exactly one of (decision order; first match wins):\n  - `graph absent` — before invoking `--check`, the skill finds the\n    `--check` script or the graph file missing\n  - `graph check failed` — the skill could not spawn/run `--check`\n    (OSError / exception before an exit code), or a subsequent `--tree`\n    exits `1` (input/IO) after a fresh `--check`\n  - `graph stale` — `--check` ran and exited non-zero (including exit `1`\n    for stale provenance and any other non-zero the script returns)\n  - `symbol not in graph` — `--tree` exited `2`\n  - `form not graph-backed` — reply used a catalogue form other than a\n    call tree (component/file/sequence/structural-diff are model-authored)\n\nOnly a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` may use the\ngrounded form. Its weakness is the opposite of ours: it trusts the model's memory of\nthe code, so a confidently wrong call tree looks identical to a right one.\n\nThis change adopts the catalogue and the brevity rules as a new prompt-only skill,\nand improves on the source in the one way this repository is positioned to: the\nsketch is **grounded** in `docs/architecture-analysis/architecture.graph.json`\nwhen the graph is fresh, via a new text export from the atlas, and **discloses its\nown coverage** on every answer — satisfying the standing codeviz principle that \"a\nvisualisation must disclose its own coverage\" (see\n`docs/proposals/codebase-visualization-tool.md`). Why now: the atlas shipped as\nPhase 0a of that proposal and its remaining phases are usage-gated; a\nquestion-driven entry point is the cheapest way to generate the usage evidence\nthat gates them, and the analysis that motivated this change is fresh.\n\n## What Changes\n\n- **New skill `skills/explain-code/`** (prompt-only, `user_invocable: true`,\n  `category: Architecture`). The atlas even lists \"show me the architecture\" as a\ntrigger, so a narrow question today either gets a wall of prose or a 650 KB page.\n\nhumanlayer's MIT-licensed `show-me` skill\n([source](https://github.com/humanlayer/skills/blob/main/plugins/show-me/skills/show-me/SKILL.md))\ndemonstrates the missing posture in about forty lines of prompt: a catalogue of\nsmall visual forms (indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree\nwith one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, structural diff,\none focused HTML file) plus five discipline rules — skip the preamble, keep prose\nbrief, pick the smallest view that makes the key point, keep only the calls and\nboundaries the current question needs, place each visual next to the text it\nsupports. Its weakness is the opposite of ours: it trusts the model's memory of\nthe code, so a confidently wrong call tree looks identical to a right one.\n\nThis change adopts the catalogue and the brevity rules as a new prompt-only skill,\nand improves on the source in the one way this repository is positioned to: the\nsketch is **grounded** in `docs/architecture-analysis/architecture.graph.json`\nwhen the graph is fresh, via a new text export from the atlas, and **discloses its\nown coverage** on every answer — satisfying the standing codeviz principle that \"a\nvisualisation must disclose its own coverage\" (see\n`docs/proposals/codebase-visualization-tool.md`). Why now: the atlas shipped as\nPhase 0a of that proposal and its remaining phases are usage-gated; a\nquestion-driven entry point is the cheapest way to generate the usage evidence\nthat gates them, and the analysis that motivated this change is fresh.\n\n## What Changes\n\n- **New skill `skills/explain-code/`** (prompt-only, `user_invocable: true`,\n  `category: Architecture`). A thin `SKILL.md` index routing to one\n  `references/<form>.md` per visual form: `call-tree.md`, `component-tree.md`,\n  `file-tree.md`, `sequence.md`, `structural-diff.md`. Each reference carries the\n  worked example adapted from humanlayer (with attribution) and the form's\n  \"smallest view\" rule. **HTML output is explicitly out of scope for v1** — the\n  skill emits text and Mermaid only, inline in the reply.\n- **Grounding step.** Before sketching, the skill checks graph freshness with\n  the existing read-only `run_architecture.py --check` (exit `0` is fresh;\n  anything else is treated as stale) and, when fresh,\n  obtains callers/callees from the new atlas `--tree` export and builds the call\n  tree from that data. When the graph is stale, absent, or does not cover the\n  files in question, the skill reads source directly and **labels the sketch\n  unverified**. It never refuses and never triggers a refresh on its own.\n- **Coverage disclosure line.** Every answer ends with one line stating the\n  grounding source (`graph @ <sha>`, or `source read, unverified`) and, for\n  grounded sketches, the per-language coverage percentage the atlas already\n  computes. The line is not optional and not collapsible.\n- **`codebase-atlas` gains `--tree <symbol-or-file> [--hops N] [--direction in|out|both]`.**\n  A stdlib-only text export in `build_atlas.py` that BFS-walks the `call` edges of\n  the existing `symbolEdges` adjacency from `build_view_model()` and prints an indented tree\n  with file path and line per node, hop-capped at 4 to match the page's slider.\n  Output is byte-stable for a fixed graph. Exit codes follow the existing\n  contract (`0` ok, `1` input error, `2` symbol not found) plus `3` for an\n  ambiguous name, which the skill resolves by asking rather than guessing.\n- **Frontmatter written for the post-`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` world.** The new\n  `SKILL.md` carries `name, description, category, tags, user_invocable, related`\n  with a description that states capability and trigger condition in third\n  person, and **omits `triggers:`**. The atlas even lists \"show me the architecture\" as a\ntrigger, so a narrow question today either gets a wall of prose or a 650 KB page.\n\nhumanlayer's MIT-licensed `show-me` skill\n([source](https://github.com/humanlayer/skills/blob/main/plugins/show-me/skills/show-me/SKILL.md))\ndemonstrates the missing posture in about forty lines of prompt: a catalogue of\nsmall visual forms (indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree\nwith one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, structural diff,\none focused HTML file) plus five discipline rules — skip the preamble, keep prose\nbrief, pick the smallest view that makes the key point, keep only the calls and\nboundaries the current question needs, place each visual next to the text it\nsupports. Its weakness is the opposite of ours: it trusts the model's memory of\nthe code, so a confidently wrong call tree looks identical to a right one.\n\nThis change adopts the catalogue and the brevity rules as a new prompt-only skill,\nand improves on the source in the one way this repository is positioned to: the\nsketch is **grounded** in `docs/architecture-analysis/architecture.graph.json`\nwhen the graph is fresh, via a new text export from the atlas, and **discloses its\nown coverage** on every answer — satisfying the standing codeviz principle that \"a\nvisualisation must disclose its own coverage\" (see\n`docs/proposals/codebase-visualization-tool.md`). Why now: the atlas shipped as\nPhase 0a of that proposal and its remaining phases are usage-gated; a\nquestion-driven entry point is the cheapest way to generate the usage evidence\nthat gates them, and the analysis that motivated this change is fresh.\n\n## What Changes\n\n- **New skill `skills/explain-code/`** (prompt-only, `user_invocable: true`,\n  `category: Architecture`). A thin `SKILL.md` index routing to one\n  `references/<form>.md` per visual form: `call-tree.md`, `component-tree.md`,\n  `file-tree.md`, `sequence.md`, `structural-diff.md`. Each reference carries the\n  worked example adapted from humanlayer (with attribution) and the form's\n  \"smallest view\" rule. **HTML output is explicitly out of scope for v1** — the\n  skill emits text and Mermaid only, inline in the reply.\n- **Grounding step.** Before sketching, the skill checks graph freshness with\n  the existing read-only `run_architecture.py --check` (exit `0` is fresh;\n  anything else is treated as stale) and, when fresh,\n  obtains callers/callees from the new atlas `--tree` export and builds the call\n  tree from that data. When the graph is stale, absent, or does not cover the\n  files in question, the skill reads source directly and **labels the sketch\n  unverified**. It never refuses and never triggers a refresh on its own.\n- **Coverage disclosure line.** Every answer ends with one line stating the\n  grounding source (`graph @ <sha>`, or `source read, unverified`) and, for\n  grounded sketches, the per-language coverage percentage the atlas already\n  computes. The line is not optional and not collapsible.\n- **`codebase-atlas` gains `--tree <symbol-or-file> [--hops N] [--direction in|out|both]`.**\n  A stdlib-only text export in `build_atlas.py` that BFS-walks the `call` edges of\n  the existing `symbolEdges` adjacency from `build_view_model()` and prints an indented tree\n  with file path and line per node, hop-capped at 4 to match the page's slider.\n  Output is byte-stable for a fixed graph. Exit codes follow the existing\n  contract (`0` ok, `1` input error, `2` symbol not found) plus `3` for an\n  ambiguous name, which the skill resolves by asking rather than guessing.\n- **Frontmatter written for the post-`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` world.** The new\n  `SKILL.md` carries `name, description, category, tags, user_invocable, related`\n  with a description that states capability and trigger condition in third\n  person, and **omits `triggers:`**. This change declares a dependency on\n  `rewrite-skill-frontmatter`; until that lands, the skill's own test asserts the\n  four surviving keys explicitly instead of calling the shared\n  `assert_required_keys_present` (which still requires `triggers`).\n- **Distribution wiring.** `skills/install-manifest.json` gains\n  `\"explain-code\": {\"distribution\": \"portable\"}` and a `cross_skill_dependencies`\n  entry `\"explain-code\": [\"codebase-atlas\", \"refresh-architecture\"]` (the validator rejects undeclared\n  `<skill-base-dir>/../` references). `skills/pyproject.toml` `testpaths` gains\n  `\"tests/explain-code\"`. The \"grounded call tree invents no symbols\" assertion lives in\n  `tests/codebase-atlas/test_atlas_tree.py` (every printed node matches a\n  fixture node by `(name, file)`). The traversal SHALL walk the symbol-level adjacency produced by `build_view_model()` (`symbolEdges`) restricted to edges whose `ty` is `call` — `import` and every other edge type are dependencies, not calls, and SHALL NOT appear as callers or callees — using only the Python standard library and making no network requests. Each line SHALL show `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`, children SHALL be sorted by name then id, a node already on the current path SHALL be printed once with the suffix `(cycle)` and not expanded, and a parent whose children exceed `--hops` SHALL carry the suffix `(+<n> more)`. The output SHALL end with a single footer line `graph @ <sha7> · <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered`, one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language present, sorted by language name and joined with ` / `, with `<percent>` printed to exactly one decimal place as `Coverage.percent` returns it (for example `14.4%`, `37.0%`), unless `--no-coverage` is given. `<target>` SHALL resolve as exact node id, then unique symbol name, then module file path or basename (rooting the tree at the module with its own symbols as hop 1). Exit codes SHALL be `0` success, `1` input or IO error, `2` target not found, `3` target ambiguous (candidate ids listed on stderr, one per line, sorted). Output SHALL be byte-identical across runs for a fixed graph and arguments.\n\n#### Scenario: Callees tree for a symbol\n\n- **WHEN** `build_atlas.py --tree <symbol-id>` runs against a graph containing that symbol\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL start with the symbol's line and list its callees indented two spaces per hop, sorted by name\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0`\n\n#### Scenario: Callers tree with hop cap\n\n- **WHEN** `--direction in --hops 1` is given for a symbol with callers two hops away\n- **THEN** only direct callers SHALL be printed\n- **AND** each printed caller that has further callers SHALL carry a `(+<n> more)` suffix\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call edges are excluded\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `A imports C`, and `--tree A --direction both` runs\n- **THEN** `B` SHALL be listed under `callees:`\n- **AND** `C` SHALL NOT appear anywhere in the output\n\n#### Scenario: Cycle is printed once\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `B calls A` and `--tree A --hops 4` runs\n- **THEN** `A` SHALL appear under `B` exactly once with the suffix `(cycle)`\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT be expanded further\n\n#### Scenario: File target gives the aggregated module view\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <file-basename>` names a module in the graph\n- **THEN** the root line SHALL be the module and hop 1 SHALL be the module's own symbols\n- **AND** subsequent hops SHALL follow those symbols' `call` edges\n\n#### Scenario: Unknown target exits 2\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a symbol that is not in the graph\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `2`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain `not found`\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous target exits 3\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a bare symbol name matching several node ids\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `3`, distinct from not-found\n- **AND** stderr SHALL list the candidate ids, one per line, sorted\n\n#### Scenario: Deterministic output\n\n- **WHEN** the same `--tree` invocation runs twice against the same graph file\n- **THEN** the two stdout outputs SHALL be byte-identical\n\n#### Scenario: Coverage footer matches the page banner\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` runs without `--no-coverage`\n- **THEN** the footer percentages SHALL equal the `Coverage.percent` values `build_view_model()` computes for the same repository root\n\n#### Scenario: Default hops and direction\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target>` is invoked with neither `--hops` nor `--direction`\n- **THEN** the traversal SHALL use `--hops 2` and `--direction out`\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0` for a resolvable target\n\n#### Scenario: Hops above four are clamped\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --hops 9` is given\n- **THEN** the effective hop cap SHALL be `4`\n- **AND** stderr SHALL contain a note that the value was clamped\n\n#### Scenario: No-coverage suppresses the footer\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <target> --no-coverage` runs\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL omit the `graph @` coverage footer line\n\n#### Scenario: Input or IO error exits 1\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` cannot read the graph file (missing path via `--graph`, or unreadable IO)\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be `1`\n\n\n#### specs/skill-workflow/spec.md\n## ADDED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: Visual Code Explainer Skill\n\nThe repository SHALL provide a user-invocable, prompt-only skill `explain-code` that answers a narrow question about the code with the smallest visual form that makes the key point clear, drawn from a fixed catalogue: indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree with one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, and structural (tree) diff. The skill SHALL keep prose brief, SHALL place each visual next to the short text it supports, and SHALL include only the calls, files, and boundaries the current question needs. The skill's `SKILL.md` SHALL be an index of at most 150 lines that links directly to one `references/<form>.md` file per visual form, with no nested reference files. In this version the skill SHALL NOT write HTML files, SHALL NOT write any file, and SHALL NOT open a browser.\n\n#### Scenario: Narrow question answered with the smallest visual\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks how a specific function, module, or message path works or connects\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL reply with exactly one visual form from the catalogue and at most three sentences of prose\n- **AND** every node in the visual SHALL carry its file location\n\n#### Scenario: Whole-repository question redirected\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL NOT render a repository-wide tree\n- **AND** it SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` as the tool for that question and stop\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive disclosure layout\n\n- **WHEN** the skill directory is inspected\n- **THEN** `SKILL.md` SHALL be at most 150 lines\n- **AND** each catalogue form SHALL have its own `references/<form>.md` reachable by a direct link from `SKILL.md`\n- **AND** no reference file SHALL link to a further reference file\n\n#### Scenario: No file or browser side effects\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers any question\n- **THEN** it SHALL emit text and Mermaid inline in the reply only\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT create, modify, or open any file\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure\n\nBefore sketching a call tree, the skill SHALL determine graph freshness by running the read-only `run_architecture.py --check` from the co-installed `refresh-architecture` skill via `<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/run_architecture.py`, treating exit code `0` alone as fresh (any non-zero exit means ungrounded; the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh). When fresh, the skill SHALL obtain callers and callees from `build_atlas.py --tree` (co-installed `codebase-atlas`) and SHALL build the call tree only from nodes that `build_atlas.py --tree` returns. When `--tree` exits `3` (ambiguous target), the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant, and SHALL NOT fall back to source reading or sketch a tree. When stale, absent, or failing (including `--tree` exit `2`), the skill SHALL read source directly and label the sketch unverified. Every sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted) SHALL end with exactly one disclosure line: `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered` when grounded (coverage list taken from the `--tree` footer by copying the substring after `· ` and before the trailing ` covered`, then re-appending ` covered`, preserving language order and ` / ` separators), or `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)` when not, where `<reason>` is chosen by first-match order: `graph absent` (script or graph missing before `--check`), `graph check failed` (`--check` could not be spawned, or `--tree` exits `1` after a fresh `--check`), `graph stale` (`--check` ran and exited non-zero), `symbol not in graph` (`--tree` exited `2`), or `form not graph-backed` (non-call-tree catalogue form). Ambiguous-symbol clarification replies and whole-repository redirect replies SHALL NOT carry a `Grounding:` line. Only a call tree built from `--tree` after a fresh `--check` MAY use the grounded form; other catalogue forms SHALL use `form not graph-backed`. The skill SHALL NOT run a refresh, `--ensure`, or the analysis pipeline itself.\n\n#### Scenario: Fresh graph grounds the call tree\n\n- **WHEN** `run_architecture.py --check` exits `0` and the question names a symbol present in the graph\n- **THEN** the call tree SHALL contain only nodes returned by `build_atlas.py --tree`\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; …` with per-language coverage percentages copied from the `--tree` footer per the substring rule above\n\n#### Scenario: Stale or absent graph falls back to source\n\n- **WHEN** `run_architecture.py --check` exits non-zero, or the script or graph file is missing\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL still answer, drawing the sketch from the source files it reads\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>)` with reason `graph stale`, `graph absent`, or `graph check failed` per the first-match order above\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT invoke `--ensure` or the analysis pipeline\n\n#### Scenario: Symbol outside graph coverage\n\n- **WHEN** the graph is fresh but `build_atlas.py --tree` exits `2` (target not found) for the requested symbol\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL fall back to source reading for that symbol\n- **AND** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (symbol not in graph)`\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call-tree form is not graph-backed\n\n- **WHEN** the skill answers with a catalogue form other than a call tree\n- **THEN** the disclosure line SHALL read `Grounding: source read, unverified (form not graph-backed)`\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT claim the grounded `graph @` form for that reply\n\n#### Scenario: Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing\n\n- **WHEN** the graph is fresh and `build_atlas.py --tree` exits `3` (ambiguous name) for the requested symbol\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL list the candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant\n- **AND** the skill SHALL NOT fall back to source reading or sketch a tree for any candidate\n- **AND** the reply SHALL NOT include a `Grounding:` line\n\n#### Scenario: Whole-repository redirect has no disclosure line\n\n- **WHEN** a user asks for the whole architecture, the full dependency graph, or a repository-wide map\n- **THEN** the skill SHALL name `/codebase-atlas` and stop\n- **AND** the reply SHALL NOT include a `Grounding:` line\n\n#### Scenario: Disclosure line present on every sketching answer\n\n- **WHEN** the skill produces a sketching reply (a catalogue visual was emitted), grounded or not\n- **THEN** the final line of the reply SHALL begin with `Grounding:`\n- **AND** the reply SHALL contain exactly one such line\n\n### Requirement: Explainer Frontmatter Without Triggers\n\nThe The traversal SHALL walk the symbol-level adjacency produced by `build_view_model()` (`symbolEdges`) restricted to edges whose `ty` is `call` — `import` and every other edge type are dependencies, not calls, and SHALL NOT appear as callers or callees — using only the Python standard library and making no network requests. Exit codes SHALL be `0` success, `1` input or IO error, `2` target not found, `3` target ambiguous (candidate ids listed on stderr, one per line, sorted). Output SHALL be byte-identical across runs for a fixed graph and arguments.\n\n#### Scenario: Callees tree for a symbol\n\n- **WHEN** `build_atlas.py --tree <symbol-id>` runs against a graph containing that symbol\n- **THEN** stdout SHALL start with the symbol's line and list its callees indented two spaces per hop, sorted by name\n- **AND** the exit code SHALL be `0`\n\n#### Scenario: Callers tree with hop cap\n\n- **WHEN** `--direction in --hops 1` is given for a symbol with callers two hops away\n- **THEN** only direct callers SHALL be printed\n- **AND** each printed caller that has further callers SHALL carry a `(+<n> more)` suffix\n\n#### Scenario: Non-call edges are excluded\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `A imports C`, and `--tree A --direction both` runs\n- **THEN** `B` SHALL be listed under `callees:`\n- **AND** `C` SHALL NOT appear anywhere in the output\n\n#### Scenario: Cycle is printed once\n\n- **WHEN** the graph contains `A calls B` and `B calls A` and `--tree A --hops 4` runs\n- **THEN** `A` SHALL appear under `B` exactly once with the suffix `(cycle)`\n- **AND** it SHALL NOT be expanded further\n\n#### Scenario: File target gives the aggregated module view\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree <file-basename>` names a module in the graph\n- **THEN** the root line SHALL be the module and hop 1 SHALL be the module's own symbols\n- **AND** subsequent hops SHALL follow those symbols' `call` edges\n\n#### Scenario: Unknown target exits 2\n\n- **WHEN** `--tree` names a symbol that is not in the graph\n- **THEN** the exit code SHALL be Neither answers a narrow question quickly. The\nsource of the adopted pattern (humanlayer `show-me`, MIT) is prompt-only and\nungrounded. This design adds the question-first entry point while keeping the\nrepository's provenance and coverage principles intact.\n\nConstraints inherited from in-flight changes (see `proposal.md` → Impact):\n`rewrite-skill-frontmatter` removes `triggers:`; `apply-progressive-disclosure-\noversized-skills` caps `SKILL.md` at 500 lines and references at one level;\n`invert-skill-test-suite-to-behavioural` wants three behavioural scenarios per\nuser-invocable skill; `collect-uncollected-skill-tests` requires a `testpaths`\nentry and forbids bare-named helper modules that collide across skills.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Prompt-only skill; the only new code is an atlas flag\n\n`skills/explain-code/` contains `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md`, no `scripts/`.\nGrounding calls `<skill-base-dir>/../codebase-atlas/scripts/build_atlas.py\n--tree`. Rationale: the catalogue works *because* it is prose (Approach 1 vs 2\nin the proposal); the one place determinism pays is the call tree, and the\natlas already holds the symbol adjacency (`build_view_model()[\"symbolEdges\"]`).\n\n### D2 — Freshness is decided by the existing `--check` contract\n\nThe skill runs `python3 \"<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/\nrun_architecture.py\" --check` and treats **exit 0 only** as fresh. Any\nnon-zero exit — the script returns `1` when provenance is not fresh, and\nother failures are also non-zero — a missing script, or a missing graph all\nmean *ungrounded*. Do **not** confuse this with `build_atlas.py --check`,\nwhich uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page; that flag is unrelated to\nexplain-code freshness. Rationale: `run_architecture.py --check` is the\nread-only half of the `architecture-refresh` contract; re-deriving freshness\nfrom `git_sha` in prose would be a second, weaker definition. The skill\n**never** runs `--ensure` or the full pipeline (proposal: \"never triggers a\nrefresh on its own\").\n\n### D3 — `--tree` output format\n\n```\nbuild_atlas.py --tree <target> [--hops N] [--direction out|in|both] [--graph PATH]\n```\n\n- Root line: `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`.\n- Children indented two spaces per hop, sorted by `name` then `id`; direction\n  `out` lists callees (`call` edges where the node is `s`), `in` lists callers, `both`\n  prints two labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`.\n- A node already printed on the current path is emitted once with the suffix\n  `(cycle)` and not expanded. A node beyond `--hops` is not printed; the parent\n  line gets the suffix `(+<n> more)` so truncation is visible.\n- `--hops` default `2`, maximum `4` (matches the page's hop slider,\n  `atlas_render.py`). Values above 4 are clamped with a stderr note.\n- Only edges with `ty == \"call\"` are walked (singular, the spelling the graph\n  uses). `symbolEdges` carries every edge type — the committed graph holds both\n  `call` and `import` edges — and an import is a dependency, not a call: walking\n  it would report importers as callers and corrupt the grounded output. A\n  dependency-tree mode over `import` edges is out of scope for this change.\n- Trailing footer, one line: `graph @ <sha7> · python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`:\n  one `<language> <percent>%` entry per language, sorted by language name, joined\n  with ` / `, percent to one decimal place (the `Coverage.percent` value\n  itself, never re-rounded, so it stays equal to the page banner), a single\n  trailing `covered`. Percentages are\n  taken from `build_view_model(measure=True)` — the same `Coverage`\n  values the page banner uses. `--no-coverage` suppresses it.\n\nDeterminism: children sorted, no timestamps, no random ids. Byte-identical for a\nfixed graph and arguments (NFR \"Determinism\").\n\n### D4 — Target resolution\n\n`<target>` resolves in this order and stops at the first hit: exact node `id`;\nunique symbol `name`; a file path or basename matching a module, in which case\nthe root is the module and hop 1 is the module's own symbols (aggregated view,\nmirroring the page's \"selecting a file gives the aggregated module view\").\nNo match exits `2` with `not found`. Ambiguous names print the candidate ids to\nstderr (one per line, sorted) and exit `3`. The two stay distinct because the\nskill must react differently: a missing symbol falls back to source reading, but\nan ambiguous one exists in the graph, so a source fallback would silently answer\nabout a guessed symbol; the skill asks which candidate was meant instead. Exit\n`1` remains input/IO errors, `0` success. Exit `3` is new for `--tree`.\n`build_atlas.py --check` already uses exit `2` for a stale HTML page;\n`--check` and `--tree` never combine on one invocation.\n\n### D5 — Disclosure line\n\nEvery **sketching** reply (a catalogue visual was emitted, grounded or not)\nends with exactly one line, never omitted, never collapsed. Two reply shapes\nare explicit exceptions and MUST NOT carry a `Grounding:` line:\n\n- **Ambiguous-symbol clarification** — `--tree` exited `3`; the skill lists\n  candidate ids and asks which was meant (no visual, no source fallback).\n- **Whole-repository redirect** — the skill names `/codebase-atlas` and stops\n  (no visual).\n\nSketching replies use one of:\n\n- grounded call tree:\n  `Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`\n  Take the `--tree` footer from D3, copy the substring after `· ` and before\n  the trailing ` covered`, then re-append ` covered`. That substring is the\n  coverage list — same language order, ` / ` separators, and one-decimal\n  percents — so the disclosure and footer cannot drift. The atlas even lists \"show me the architecture\" as a\ntrigger, so a narrow question today either gets a wall of prose or a 650 KB page.\n\nhumanlayer's MIT-licensed `show-me` skill\n([source](https://github.com/humanlayer/skills/blob/main/plugins/show-me/skills/show-me/SKILL.md))\ndemonstrates the missing posture in about forty lines of prompt: a catalogue of\nsmall visual forms (indented call tree, component tree with file paths, file tree\nwith one-line responsibility comments, Mermaid sequence diagram, structural diff,\none focused HTML file) plus five discipline rules — skip the preamble, keep prose\nbrief, pick the smallest view that makes the key point, keep only the calls and\nboundaries the current question needs, place each visual next to the text it\nsupports. Its weakness is the opposite of ours: it trusts the model's memory of\nthe code, so a confidently wrong call tree looks identical to a right one.\n\nThis change adopts the catalogue and the brevity rules as a new prompt-only skill,\nand improves on the source in the one way this repository is positioned to: the\nsketch is **grounded** in `docs/architecture-analysis/architecture.graph.json`\nwhen the graph is fresh, via a new text export from the atlas, and **discloses its\nown coverage** on every answer — satisfying the standing codeviz principle that \"a\nvisualisation must disclose its own coverage\" (see\n`docs/proposals/codebase-visualization-tool.md`). Why now: the atlas shipped as\nPhase 0a of that proposal and its remaining phases are usage-gated; a\nquestion-driven entry point is the cheapest way to generate the usage evidence\nthat gates them, and the analysis that motivated this change is fresh.\n\n## What Changes\n\n- **New skill `skills/explain-code/`** (prompt-only, `user_invocable: true`,\n  `category: Architecture`). A thin `SKILL.md` index routing to one\n  `references/<form>.md` per visual form: `call-tree.md`, `component-tree.md`,\n  `file-tree.md`, `sequence.md`, `structural-diff.md`. Each reference carries the\n  worked example adapted from humanlayer (with attribution) and the form's\n  \"smallest view\" rule. **HTML output is explicitly out of scope for v1** — the\n  skill emits text and Mermaid only, inline in the reply.\n- **Grounding step.** Before sketching, the skill checks graph freshness with\n  the existing read-only `run_architecture.py --check` (exit `0` is fresh;\n  anything else is treated as stale) and, when fresh,\n  obtains callers/callees from the new atlas `--tree` export and builds the call\n  tree from that data. When the graph is stale, absent, or does not cover the\n  files in question, the skill reads source directly and **labels the sketch\n  unverified**. It never refuses and never triggers a refresh on its own.\n- **Coverage disclosure line.** Every answer ends with one line stating the\n  grounding source (`graph @ <sha>`, or `source read, unverified`) and, for\n  grounded sketches, the per-language coverage percentage the atlas already\n  computes. The line is not optional and not collapsible.\n- **`codebase-atlas` gains `--tree <symbol-or-file> [--hops N] [--direction in|out|both]`.**\n  A stdlib-only text export in `build_atlas.py` that BFS-walks the `call` edges of\n  the existing `symbolEdges` adjacency from `build_view_model()` and prints an indented tree\n  with file path and line per node, hop-capped at 4 to match the page's slider.\n  Output is byte-stable for a fixed graph.
